Port's clear — iteration 10 loads on open. I've carried in all your edge decisions. Let me walk you through them.

---

**1. A large library — Load more & sorting** → **[http://maker:4001/?demo=many](http://maker:4001/?demo=many)** (300 links)
- The list shows a manageable batch, then a **Load more (…)** button at the bottom — click it to bring in the next batch. No page numbers.
- Look at the **All** tab count (the full total) and then type **sample** in search: the results line reports **every** match across the whole library, even though only a batch is drawn on screen. So **search, tag filters, and counts always cover everything**, not just what's loaded.
- Top-right there's a **Sort** control — switch between **Newest added / Oldest added / Title (A–Z)** and watch the order change.

**2. Long content** → **[http://maker:4001/?demo=long](http://maker:4001/?demo=long)**
- The **title now wraps to two lines** before shortening, so distinguishing detail isn't lost.
- The long note shows a **preview with "Show full note"** — click to expand it in place, "Show less" to collapse. No need to open Edit just to read it.

**3. Dates** — in the *many* demo, sort by **Oldest added**: the oldest entries (older than about a week) show an **actual date**, while recent saves stay relative ("3 h ago"). Dates include the year when it isn't the current year.

A few choices to confirm:

- **Sort is a small dropdown** with those three orders. Is a dropdown the right control, and are those the orders you need — or would you also want something like "recently read"?
- **Load more brings ~25 at a time.** Is that a comfortable batch size?
- The **long-note preview** kicks in past a certain length. Does the preview height feel about right?

If these settle well, that completes the edge exploration across every part — and I'll summarize the whole settled scope and ask whether to start building the real thing.
